summary.short: Creates a federal property-type right in an individual's voice and visual likeness, making unauthorized digital replicas and products designed to produce them actionable in civil suits, with notice-and-takedown and safe-harbor rules for online services. Effective 180 days after enactment.
summary.long: The bill creates a federal intellectual property right in the voice and visual likeness of individuals. The right is not assignable during life, is licensable, and does not expire on death; it is exclusive to the individual and to a right holder for 10 years after death, extendable by 5-year periods subject to public use, and terminates at the earlier of non-renewal or 70 years after death. Lifetime licenses are limited to 10 years (5 years for a living minor, court approval required for minors) and must be written, signed and describe intended uses; collective bargaining agreements are excepted. Anyone who, affecting interstate commerce, makes available an unauthorized digital replica, or distributes, imports or markets a product primarily designed to produce digital replicas of identified individuals, is liable in a civil action. Remedies are the greater of statutory amounts (from 5,000 dollars per work for individuals, up to 750,000 dollars per work or product for online providers that have not made a good faith compliance effort) or actual damages and profits; punitive damages are available for willful conduct. Online services that adopt a repeat-violator termination policy, designate an agent with the Copyright Office, and remove material on valid notice receive safe harbor. Knowingly false notices incur liability of at least 25,000 dollars per notification. Bona fide news, documentary, commentary, parody and fleeting uses are excluded, except sexually explicit depictions. Actions must be brought within 3 years of discovery, and state-law claims are preempted with stated exceptions. Liability applies to conduct after enactment.

notes: Introduced text of S. 1367 (April 9, 2025; referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee). The text does not amend, repeal or implement any existing U.S. Code provision, and states no legal_basis; it creates a new federal civil cause of action (Sec. 2(e)). Cross-referenced instruments are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Sec. 2(j)(1)(A) limits liability to conduct after enactment, while Sec. 2(j)(2)(A) applies the digital replication right to individuals who die before or after enactment; these address different things and are not inconsistent. Sec. 2(k) sets effect 180 days after enactment. Relations section_status is recorded only because the schema requires it; relation rows are present.
